ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories against: Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list; UN Security Council Consolidated List; EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; US OFAC SDN List; UK HMT consolidated list; and international PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory when any UBO, director or representative is classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), including family members and close associates. All results must be documented and retained for at least 10 years under AMLA and Swiss Code of Obligations arts. 370a et seq. For a medium-risk enhanced business (interactive audio chatroom with Apple/Google in-app payments), the responsible incorporation agent must obtain certified identity evidence and independently verify the source of funds before filing the incorporation deed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), operated by the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office; actual name reservation and registration are effected through the competent Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin characters; names in Cyrillic, Han characters or other non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script. The name may be chosen in German, French, Italian, Romansh or another language, provided it is pronounceable in Swiss practice, does not mislead the public, and is distinct within the entire Swiss Commercial Register. The legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' (German) / 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' (French) / 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' (Italian) is mandatory. For a multilingual AG, a combined suffix such as 'AG/SA' may be registered.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Banco, Banca, Sparkasse – requires FINMA banking licence
Insurance, Assurance, Versicherung, Assicurazione – requires FINMA insurance supervision
Swiss, Suisse, Schweiz, Svizzera, Helvetia, Helvetic – requires special authorization under Swissness/naming protection
Federal, Confederation, Bund, Eidgenossenschaft, Canton, Commune – requires state or cantonal authorization
Trust – restricted and subject to enhanced scrutiny; requires demonstration of genuine trust services and professional domicile
Foundation, Stiftung, Fondation – cannot be used as a suffix for an AG and requires the legal form of a foundation
Audit, Revision, Revisionsgesellschaft – requires audit licensing in accordance with Swiss auditing supervision rules
Handelsbank, Investmentfund, Private Equity – requires FINMA or financial supervisory authorization
University, Hochschule, Institut – may require cantonal educational authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must obtain the written refusal with reasons from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office. Within 10 working days of receipt, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsicht / Autorité de surveillance du registre du commerce), submitting a corrected alternative name or a legal memorandum. The supervisory authority may issue a decision confirming or overturning the refusal. Within 30 days of that decision, the appellant may appeal to the cantonal superior court and, on Federal law grounds, to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court. Alternative administrative remedy: immediately re-submit a revised name through the same registry portal, which may be expedited at cantonal discretion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual office or P.O.-Box-only registered office is not permissible; the Articles of Association must disclose a specific physical street address within Switzerland where the AG is actually administered, and where service of process and official correspondence can be made. However, a professional domiciliation service (Sitzbüro / bureau fiduciaire) with a physical office, local personnel and file access rights is permissible and commonly accepted, provided it does not constitute a sham/letterbox entity and is not used to circumvent Swiss administrative oversight.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a medium-risk enhanced interactive audio and companion social app, the annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is estimated at 35% to 40%, increasing to approximately 60% if the company uses an external registered-agent-only address without substantial local management or operational records in Switzerland. Cantonal commercial-Register offices, social security authorities, and tax inspectors retain the right to conduct unannounced inspections to verify actual seat, UBO documentation and commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 626-763 (Stock Corporation Law); Article 640 (registered office); Articles 644-652 (board of directors and auditors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), with central publication via the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC) and the Zefix register portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted via the statutory 'Anmeldung zur Eintragung' application form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 112,000). At least 20% of the nominal capital, i.e. CHF 20,000, must be fully paid up and deposited in a blocked (liberation) account with a Swiss bank, to remain blocked until the Commercial Register issues the registration extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1) The share subscription and payment plan be approved; the paid-up share capital of CHF 20,000 is confirmed as deposited in a blocked account with a Swiss bank. 2) The registered office of the Company is established at Löwenstrasse 1, 6300 Zug, Switzerland. 3) The following persons are appointed: [Name Surname] as Chairwoman of the Board of Directors, [Name Surname] as Chief Executive Officer, and [Name Surname] as Company Secretary and AML Officer. 4) The Board determines organisation regulations, delegates day-to-day management to the CEO, and authorises the officers to procure the entry of the Company in the Commercial Register, open bank accounts and publish the required notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Notary Public of the Canton of Zug (Cantonal Notariat Zug).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the deed of incorporation, Articles of Association, subscription list for shares, list of founders, declarations on paid-up capital and powers of board members. The notary verifies the identity of all founders and board members, reads the instrument aloud, and authenticates their signatures.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each founder and board member
Declaration of share subscriptions and nominal amounts
Criminal record extract or declaration of no restrictions for officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the capital schedule or powers of attorney, amend the subscription schedule and re-notarize before submitting the application to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-up Capital Deposit in a Blocked Swiss Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank located in the Canton of Zug (e.g. Zuger Kantonalbank or a licensed private bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked corporation formation account (AG-Liberationskonto) in the name of the future company, transfer the required CHF 20,000 from founders' accounts, and obtain the bank's blocking confirmation (Freigabebestätigung or Sperrguthaben-Bestätigung) stating that the funds are at the company's disposal upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed and Articles of Association
Initial capital deposit payment order or bank transfer reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the block account or issues a query, provide complete source-of-funds evidence under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and re-submit the application with corrected beneficiary data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt) via the Swiss Commercial Register electronic portal (SOG).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung) with the fully executed notarial deed, bank blocking confirmation, officer specimen signatures, and confirmation of the registered office. The registry reviews the legality and completeness of the filing and issues an entry in the Commercial Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency order (Verfügung), remedy the stated omissions within 10 days, pay any amendment fee and refile; appeal to the Cantonal Court of Appeal within 30 days in case of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Statistics Registration (UID, VAT, Employer Duties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (BfS/Neuchâtel) and the Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug; Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV) for VAT.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Commercial Register extract and enterprise identification number (UID). Register for value added tax if annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000; register with the cantonal equalization fund for AHV/AVS employer contributions and the accident insurance provider (e.g. Suva) for personnel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused or delayed, re-apply with clarifications and obtain the formal decision, then appeal to the respective cantonal or federal tax authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette and Opening of Operational Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC) and the Company's corporate bank in Switzerland.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the Commercial Register entry is published in the SOGC. Open the operational corporate bank account using the registration extract and UID certificate. Issue the share certificates and maintain the share register, return the blocked funds to the company treasury after full release, and file annual statutory reports.
required_dossiers: SOGC publication proof or entry reference
First board resolution approving bank signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SOGC publication fails, request a republication from the registry; if the bank rejects the operational account application, supplement the UBO declaration and business plan or select an alternative licensed bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no physical industrial installation; the activity is a digital voice streaming and social application operated from a Swiss registered office with cloud infrastructure.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - ISIC 6311 (data processing, hosting and related activities) is not subject to a Cantonal industrial manufacturing licence in Switzerland.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN, BAFU) and Cantonal Office of Environment (Zug).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for the app operator; no own production plant or stationary emissions source. Server hosting is outsourced to certified Swiss data centers subject to their own permitting obligations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct wastewater or VOC discharge from the company's operations. The company must ensure its data center partners comply with the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV) and the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV), including server room cooling efficiency and waste heat recovery obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and inspection by the Cantonal Fire Insurance (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) required for the registered office and office premises; workplace clearance from Suva (Swiss National Accident Insurance) for office-based staff. No civil-defense construction clearance applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV – Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung), Bern; online e-services portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch. Cantonal and communal tax authorities (e.g., Kantonales Steueramt) administer direct taxes, while the commercial register authority (Handelsregisteramt) issues the UID business identification number. The Swiss Customs Authority (FOCBS/BAZG) administers customs declarations and export proofs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) must: (1) execute the notarial deed of incorporation and appoint the board of directors; (2) register the AG in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) of the canton of registered office; on entry, the Federal Statistical Office automatically assigns the 9-digit Swiss Business Identification Number (UID, format CHE-123.456.789), which serves as the corporate tax ID; (3) for VAT purposes, complete VAT registration with the ESTV through the e-services portal (ePortal/eService) once annual taxable turnover from Swiss-domestic supplies reaches CHF 100,000 (effective 1 January 2025, lowered from CHF 250,000); (4) obtain the MWST/VAT number (CHE-123.456.789 MWST) and file quarterly or semi-annual returns electronically. Foreign entities not domiciled in Switzerland and registering for Swiss VAT must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (domiciliary representative) and submit the ESTV's 'Registration of a foreign company' form, including articles of incorporation, board/power-of-attorney evidence, and ISIC business activity codes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Swiss AG is a separate legal person subject to unlimited corporate income tax liability at the federal, cantonal, and communal levels based on registered office (Sitz) or place of effective management in Switzerland. It is not a pass-through entity; shareholders are taxed separately on distributions. Territorial scope: worldwide income of the AG is taxable, with double-tax-treaty relief and the Swiss domestic carve-outs for foreign permanent establishments and foreign real estate; no tax-exempt zone treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law contains no US-style check-the-box election, but provides the following legally binding elections/reliefs: (i) participation deduction (Beteiligungsabzug) election for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from substantial shareholdings (≥10% or fair-market-value threshold CHF 1 million); (ii) patent box and R&D super-deduction elections available in most cantons; (iii) mandatory tax ruling requests with cantonal and federal authorities to confirm transfer pricing, permanent-establishment avoidance, and financing structures; (iv) hybrid mismatch outcome adjustments (Swiss rules effective 1 January 2020 implementing BEPS Action 2) disallow deductions for hybrid arrangements resulting in double non-taxation and deny election benefits; (v) VAT optional net-rate method (Saldomethode) election for taxpayers with turnover below CHF 5,005,000 (subject to requirements); (vi) election to file Swiss VAT Group (Gruppenbesteuerung) for qualifying affiliated entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / TVA) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (Bundesgesetz über die Mehrwertsteuer, MWSTG), administered centrally by the ESTV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover from Swiss-domestic supplies, effective 1 January 2025 (previously CHF 250,000). The threshold applies cumulatively across the AG's total Swiss taxable supplies; foreign suppliers of electronically supplied services (including voice-streaming and digital services) to private consumers domiciled in Switzerland must register for Swiss VAT even below the threshold, unless the electronic interface operator (Apple/Google) is deemed the supplier under the 1 January 2025 Schnittstellengesetz platform framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital tax stamping, or API-based invoice clearance regime for private documents. Mandatory invoice elements include supplier name and MWST/UID, recipient name and address, date, description of supply, consideration, and applicable VAT rate/amount. Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) acceptance has been mandatory for domestic B2B/B2C invoice payments since 30 June 2020. A structured B2B e-invoicing mandate (eBill/Peppol-similar XML format) becomes generally binding on 1 January 2026 (voluntary adoption since 2024; EDI legacy formats remain acceptable). VAT returns are filed digitally via the ESTV e-service portal under a self-assessment system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (i) export of movable goods abroad substantiated by a Swiss customs export declaration; (ii) services the recipient uses outside Switzerland (export of services) under Article 23(2) and place-of-supply rules of Article 18 MWSTG, including electronically supplied services (voice streaming, digital content) supplied to business or private recipients domiciled abroad; (iii) ancillary transport services linked to exported goods; and (iv) certain international services. For the voice-streaming social app, in-app purchases settled through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing to foreign end customers may be zero-rated if Swiss supply-side rules apply and substantiation proves recipient residence abroad (billing address, IP geo-location, payment-card BIN, and subscriber contract data). Supplies to residents of Switzerland are subject to Swiss VAT at 8.1%; where the App Store/Google Play operator is deemed the supplier under the 2025 electronic-interface rules, the platform is liable for Swiss VAT on B2C digital supplies, requiring the AG to structure contract flows accordingly.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Zollanmeldung / déclaration en douane) accepted by the FOCBS/BAZG
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (transport document evidencing physical export)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or payment-provider credit confirmation showing FX repatriation of export proceeds)
Commercial invoice and underlying export/service contract
Recipient-domicile evidence for services (IP log data, payment card BIN, business registration extract, or signed recipient confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV may audit export zero-rating substantiation at any time within a 10-year VAT assessment limitation period. Unsubstantiated zero-rating claims are retrospectively recharacterized as taxable domestic supplies, with VAT assessed at 8.1%, plus interest applied from the filing date. Under Articles 103–105 MWSTG, penalties for tax evasion are imposed: up to 15% of the tax evaded for negligent conduct, up to 25% for intentional conduct, and in aggravated cases or for VAT fraud (Abgabebetrug), a fine of up to CHF 30,000 and imprisonment of up to 2 years may be imposed on responsible directors; clawback of input VAT credits previously taken is also mandatory.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF), with the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) supervising banking and payment institutions for compliance purposes
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc (CHF) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Switzerland maintains no foreign exchange controls, no surrender requirements, no import deposit schemes, and no central bank approval for cross-border fund movements. Dividends, royalties, interest and loan repayments may be freely remitted abroad, subject only to the 35% statutory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) or applicable treaty relief. Capital repatriation is unrestricted, but all payments must comply with Swiss sanctions law, anti-money laundering (AMLA) requirements, and the transparency obligations of the Swiss Financial Market Supervision. In practice, banks treat crypto-origin funds, non-verified beneficial owners, or high-risk counterparties as the principal friction points rather than any FX restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Switzerland imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. A Swiss AG may hold foreign currency in its accounts freely, use it for offshore trade settlements, or defer conversion, as the national treatment under the SNB's free capital movement principle presumes unrestricted foreign exchange handling. Banks will nonetheless record the current-account underlying and may request export invoices to evidence the commercial purpose of an incoming payment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for registered estate capital deposit) and Operational Multcurrency Account in CHF/EUR/USD
Funding Escrow Account and Operational Clearing Account with SIC/EURO SIC and SWIFT connectivity
Operational Account for treasury and royalty payments; dedicated Capital Deposit Account
CHF Operational Account and segregated Client Funds Account (if app/treasury receives customer balances)
Tier-1 cooperative bank account for payroll, VAT and operational liquidity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium as a supplemental treasury rail but Low as the primary clearing route. An EU/UK-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) cannot passport into Switzerland; it may offer a CHF settlement through a Swiss correspondent bank, yet such an arrangement does not grant direct SIC membership and fails the Swiss-payment prudential test. FINMA-registered Swiss fintech firms or SRO members can serve as secondary wallets for small user refunds, loyalty payouts, and cash-flow ring-fencing, but the core cross-border treasury should remain on tier-1 Swiss banks to guarantee direct CHF clearing, foreign exchange pricing, and repo-style liquidity. A pure digital EMI opening without physical Swiss nexus is not acceptable for a medium-risk app revenue treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss tier-1 banks and cantonal banks require physical presence of at least one director (and normally the AML responsible officer) for the first account-opening interview. Exceptions exist only where the existing relationship is already at level 4, the company is a joint venture of an established bank client, or the bank offers a regulated remote onboarding app after intense video-verified KYC; in practice no fully remote opening is available for a newly incorporated AG with digital-media monetisation. At least one director must attend a face-to-face meeting in Switzerland, bring original identity documents, and the ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more must be disclosed with a certified excerpt from the Swiss Commercial Register. Companies with a non-resident board or a foreign holding structure may be approved only after additional source-of-funds evidence and independent legal opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high volume of consumer micro-transactions from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing received on a daily basis, which can be misclassified as fragmented cash deposits or potential micro-laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) signed platform agreements with Apple and Google including Merchant ID and App Store Connect identifier; (2) monthly transaction volume reports in CSV/JSON format from in-app purchase platforms; (3) audited reconciliation of gross billings vs net proceeds to operating accounts; (4) documented refund and dispute lifecycle policy; (5) liquidity-flow diagram showing consumer payments route only via platform payout before reaching the Swiss treasury account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: virtual voice-streaming credits, gift tokens and tipping features obscure beneficial ownership and the underlying content, creating a potential channel for value transfer to unspecified third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (1) a detailed business model description with a service flowchart and user consent terms; (2) anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing risk assessment specifically covering virtual credits and gifting; (3) transaction monitoring rules that block suspicious patterns, velocity thresholds and account-to-account transfers; (4) token lifecycle white-paper explaining purchase, consumption, expiry, no-money-launder and no-cash-redemption clauses; (5) audited proof that consumer credit purchases are non-redeemable for cash outside the licensed payment rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: ultimate beneficial owners or shareholder funds originating from a Crypto Valley / digital-asset structure, with potential unavailability of conventional source-of-wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) full UBO registry declaration through the official Swiss Register of Beneficial Owners; (2) notarised source-of-wealth statement supported by crypto exchange transaction history, bank statements, or audit reports; (3) certified chain-of-title over the digital currency showing initial purchase and conversion route; (4) legal opinion on the validity of the financing and any Swiss securities law implications; (5) confirmation from an external audit firm that the assets have legitimate origin and are not derived from sanctions-tainted wallets or darknet markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: the app serves a global customer base with IP addresses from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, creating cross-border sanctions and correspondent-bank rejection exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) geographic blocking list and geo-IP enforcement policy; (2) an up-to-date sanctions screening policy referencing SECO, unload and OFAC lists; (3) KYC verification for high-risk customers including recognised passport proof and PEP screening; (4) transaction monitoring rules for high-risk country traffic; (5) legal commitment letter from counsel confirming no services are delivered to sanctioned or Russian/Crimean/Iranian/Cuban/North-Korean territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: cross-border royalty payments to a related foreign distributor or parent company without apparent commercial substance, triggering transfer-pricing and possible hidden-value-transfer inquiries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (1) a transfer-pricing documentation report applying the OECD transfer-pricing guidelines and Switzerland-authored Country-by-Country requirements; (2) executed IP licensing agreements with economic substance and royalty-rate benchmarking; (3) the Swiss AG's operational substance file comprising board meeting minutes, payroll records and office premises; (4) audited intercompany en-documentation for any deductible royalties; (5) historically forecasted cash-flow statements demonstrating that royalty outflow corresponds to engineering and content-streaming services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 or domestic SIC payment in CHF from the shareholder's bank. The transaction narrative must contain the ISO 20022 purpose code appropriate to the inflow, typically 'DIMG' (Direct Investment - Foreign) for equity or 'COMC' for intra-group commercial funding, and must reference the executed shareholder resolution, articles of association or capital increase deed. The receiving Swiss bank requires a sworn source-of-funds declaration for the amount and will place a ring-fenced credit hold until the Commercial Register ('Handelsregisteramt') confirms the capital encumbrance release. For foreign-currency injections, the bank may require an intra-group treasury confirmation and a reason for the foreign currency; in all cases exchange-rate risk is contemporaneously hedged via FX forward.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements use SWIFT MT103 / PACS.008 for ordinary supplier and tax payments, MT202 for bank-to-bank reimbursements, and confirmed irrevocable commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) for high-value, documentary trade settlements. CHF-denominated instructions are cleared via SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing), EUR payments via EURO SIC, and USD through correspondent banks with UBS/OCBC or another major New-York clearing correspondent. The treasury beneficiary of a payment gateway must maintain segregated sub-accounts for (i) platform fees, (ii) content royalties, (iii) VAT / Swiss WHT settlements, (iv) payroll and (v) litigation reserves; each sub-ledger should have its own MT101 instruction batch and reference number to enable straight-through reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, GBP/CHF) for anticipated commodity and trade flows
FX Swap (combined spot and forward operation) to bridge between CHF funding and USD/EUR disbursement cycles
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) on a limited set of non-convertible emerging-market currencies, operating strictly on a cash-settlement basis under ISDA terms with a Swiss/G7 bank counterparty
Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) to fix long-term USD or EUR revenue streams against CHF liabilities in the parental capital structure
OTC European-Style FX Options (put/call) bought for hedging downside on large tender receivables; premium payment is limited and no leveraged speculative sale is permitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Federal and Cantonal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and Cantonal Tax Administration (Steuerverwaltung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March after the fiscal year-end; extensions to 30 June or 30 September on application (standard for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at approximately 5% per annum; late-filing penalties reaching 25-30% of assessed tax; estimated assessment by the authority; evasion penalties up to three times the evaded tax (intent) or one-third (negligence).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each quarter-end; annual return within 60 days after year-end if turnover below CHF 100,000 (exclusive of VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum; procedural fines up to CHF 800; evasion penalties up to 100% of evaded VAT (intentional cases higher); non-remittance creates personal director exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding Tax (Verrechnungssteuer) Declaration and Remittance on Dividends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Withholding Tax Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each calendar quarter-end (30 April, 31 July, 31 October, 31 January); due only upon actual dividend distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% per annum; penalty up to the amount of unreported withheld tax; criminal liability of board members in aggravated cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AHV/OASI Annual Wage Statement and Contribution Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January following the calendar year for electronic filing; 28/29 February for paper-based statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest at 5% per annum; administrative fines up to CHF 10,000; criminal sanctions for false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting and Shareholder Approval of Annual Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' General Meeting (internal corporate body; no government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors jointly and severally liable for damages resulting from non-approval; commercial register authority may order compliance and, upon persistent default, initiate strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Audited Annual Accounts, Audit Report, and SOGC Publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the balance-sheet date; mandatory only for companies subject to ordinary audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Register-compulsion fines; adverse SOGC notice; administrative strike-off after formal statutory warning for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register Update of Corporate Particulars (Directors, Share Capital, Powers of Signature, Registered Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Without undue delay after the underlying corporate act; event-triggered, not an annual renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Order-compliant fines (Ordnungsbusse); defaulting board members liable for damages; prolonged failure can trigger strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is required if two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets above CHF 20 million; sales revenue above CHF 40 million; annual average above 250 full-time employees. Companies with fewer than 10 employees may permanently opt out of both ordinary and limited audit; otherwise a limited audit (review) applies unless shareholders appoint an ordinary auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b) for statutory annual accounts; Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS acceptable for statutory and consolidated accounts; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER mandatory for consolidated reporting of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland requires no public annual UBO filing. Since the 2023 company-law reform, bearer shareholders must disclose their identity to the AG within one month; the AG records beneficial owners in a non-public register (Verzeichnis der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten) kept at the registered office and available to tax and AML authorities on request. Registered-shareholder entries in the Aktienbuch must be current and are certified at each AGM; any dividend payment requires a 35% withholding-tax declaration to ESTV.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Officers with Powers of Signature (Verzeichnis des Verwaltungsrats)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct tax 8.5% on net profit (effective 7.83% after deductibility of federal tax itself) plus cantonal and communal corporate income tax; combined all-in statutory headline rate for an AG in Canton Zug is approximately 14.6%, while the national cantonal blended range is approximately 12%–21% depending on the canton of residence.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory and administrative incentives include participation exemption for dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholdings (>=10% or market value >= CHF 1 million), cantonal notional interest deduction on qualifying equity, patent box relief in participating cantons, R&D super-deduction up to 150% in certain cantons, holding and principal company regimes, and reorganization rollover relief. No general tax holidays are available for ordinary AGs, but cantonal investment rulings may produce mid-single-digit effective rates in qualifying cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal and federal corporate income tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration d'impôt personnes morales) filed through SwissTax/eTax or the canton's authorized e-filing channel, e.g. Zug's official portal. The federal direct tax section is contained within the same combined return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. One return per business year. If the financial year differs from the calendar year, the return follows the business year-end and includes opening asset and equity reconciliations. Additional schedules, forms and valuation statements are due together with the return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due no later than six months after the company's fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the usual cantonal deadline is 31 March of the following year, with an administrative extension to 31 October commonly granted when a qualified representative is engaged. In Zug, the standard deadline for calendar-year accounts is 30 June unless an extension is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, Swiss UID number, commercial register number, legal form (AG/SA), registered office address, date of incorporation, fiscal year-end and principal purpose.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlling shareholders must be fully identified in an appendix with name, residence, ownership percentage and position; a Swiss resident registered agent or director must be named and available for service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet in CHF: share capital, legal reserves, retained earnings, shareholders' equity, financial liabilities, receivables from shareholders/affiliates, intangible assets and all operating assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned AGs must attach complete statutory accounts including notes; shareholder loans must be separately disclosed. English-only accounts should be accompanied by a German, French or Italian translation if requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Net profit per commercial accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit before taxes as reported in the statutory income statement, reconciled to the balance-sheet change in equity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No adjustment is made merely because shareholders are non-residents; Swiss statutory accounting rules apply fully. Profits attributable to foreign shareholders remain taxable in Switzerland unless a permanent-establishment allocation is properly documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses and recognition of deductible items: hidden profit distributions, personal expenses, excessive director compensation, interest on excessive shareholder debt, tax penalties, political contributions and similar items are added back; participation deductions, previous-year losses and IP relief are subtracted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, any non-arm's-length payment for management services, royalties, license fees, commissions or interest is characterized as a constructive dividend, subject to Swiss withholding tax and personal-liability consequences unless fully disclosed and priced accurately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit for federal corporate income tax after application of federal-level deductions, participation relief and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholder residency does not alter the federal taxable base of the Swiss AG; the AG is a Swiss-resident taxpayer and the full federal tax is assessed at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 21 / Cantonal and communal tax profit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit for cantonal/communal corporate income tax after application of cantonal rate schedules and incentives such as patent box, NID, R&D deductions and participation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should ensure any cantonal tax mix or substance ruling is attached and supported by operating facts in Switzerland; reliance on incentives without real activity triggers reopening and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declared taxable equity for capital-tax purposes, including share capital, disclosed reserves and retained earnings; used for cantonal capital tax and hidden-reserve assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loans made by non-resident shareholders in lieu of equity must be documented via a written loan agreement at arm's-length interest; repeated repayments or waived interest may be recharacterized as taxable equity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing produces an administrative reminder and coercive order, a procedural fine of up to CHF 10,000, and potential loss of deduction rights. Intentional false statements constitute tax evasion and attract a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax, plus interest at 5% per annum. Aggravated tax fraud may result in criminal prosecution and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% on any dividend, profit share, constructive distribution and economically equivalent distribution made by a Swiss AG, regardless of shareholder residence. In-kind distributions, including platform credits, virtual benefits or creditor waivers, are also within scope if capable of monetary valuation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder seeking reduced dividend withholding tax under a DTA must be the beneficial owner and satisfy any ownership threshold and holding-period condition. The shareholder must file a Swiss withholding tax refund application (Form 823B / R-82) with the FTA within three years of payment and attach a valid tax residence certificate (TRC), audited documentation of shareholding and a declaration of beneficial ownership. An advance treaty-rate ruling can be obtained before payment for material or ongoing distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law generally does not impose WHT on outgoing ordinary royalties or interest on commercial loans. However, interest on Swiss bonds, bank deposits and collective investment units is subject to statutory 35% WHT. Under DTAs, royalties and ordinary debt interest are typically exempt or subject to reduced rates of 0%–10%, but substance and beneficial-ownership tests apply; payments recharacterized as dividends remain subject to 35% unless treaty reduced.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF; administrative practice applies materiality thresholds in CHF. A Master File is broadly expected where the consolidated group's revenue exceeds CHF 1 billion, and a Local File is expected where the Swiss entity's annual turnover exceeds CHF 50 million or where individual related-party transaction categories exceed CHF 1 million per annum. Exact thresholds follow Swiss Tax Conference guidance and FTA enforcement practice under OECD standards.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not maintain offshore-style ESR codes. Instead, Swiss tax law and treaty practice impose an economic-substance requirement through beneficial ownership, actual place of management, substantive business purpose and profit-allocation standards under the OECD Guidelines and the MLI Principal Purpose Test. For a voice-streaming app, the Swiss AG must demonstrate genuine management, contracted operating personnel, product-specific decision-making, platform/system hosting in Switzerland and real administrative substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and intentional false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating gross revenue from in-app subscriptions, virtual gifts or digital audio credits; recording fake shareholder loans; suppressing payment-rail reports received from Apple or Google; altering invoices; or concealing foreign-controlled accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Simple tax evasion is punishable by a penalty up to three times the evaded tax, plus interest on the underpayment. Aggravated tax fraud is a criminal tax offense and carries fines calculated from the evaded amount and, in serious cases, imprisonment for up to five years. Tax authorities may reopen prior years, disallow loss carryforwards and issue discretionary assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers and shadow managers having actual control who sign or facilitate false returns are personally subject to evaded-tax penalties, civil restitution and criminal conviction. Travel bans, asset seizure, entry restrictions and imprisonment may be imposed against natural persons even if the corporation remains liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and abusive treaty structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG as a letterbox company with no local management, no payroll, no offices, no operational contracts and no real decision-making; using Swiss shell vehicles to interpose royalty flows from a voice-platform business conducted abroad; obtaining tax rulings through materially false substance declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FTA and cantons may disregard the corporate form, allocate income to the true economic owner, deny DTA exemption and treaty benefits, cancel protective rulings, reclassify transactions as constructive dividends and impose penalties up to three times the evaded tax. The commercial register authority may also order the company's liquidation if the required registered seat and actual administration are not maintained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who lack authority, fail to carry out management functions or accept instructions from undisclosed principals are jointly and severally liable for tax debts. Foreign beneficial owners may be subjected to extradition-backed investigations, entry bans and personal civil judgments for the AG's non-payment of taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify traders and commercial users transacting through the voice-streaming application; accepting payments from criminal counterparts through IAP or Play Billing without AML procedures; failing to file suspicious activity reports with MROS; ignoring beneficial-ownership disclosure duties; crossing into FINMA-regulated payment or e-money activities without authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering under Article 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years, or up to five years in qualified cases, plus confiscation of assets. FINMA may issue enforcement orders, terminate unlawful payment activity, impose fines and prohibit individuals. Administrative fines of up to CHF 500,000 per person and corporate penalties also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, money-laundering officers and beneficial owners are personally prosecutable. Arrests, travel bans, freezing of personal assets and imprisonment are possible. Jurisdiction over remotely located founders may be asserted through Swiss mutual legal assistance and international arrest requests.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax failure on profit repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying or crediting dividends, constructive profit distributions, excessive interest or excessively high royalty-like payments for user-generated content licenses without collecting the statutory 35% withholding tax; failing to obtain pre-authorization for treaty-reduced rates; or accounting for distributions as tax-neutral advances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Federal Tax Administration may enforce collection of the full 35% WHT from the AG, with late-payment interest at 5% per annum and administrative fines. If the transaction is recharacterized as a hidden distribution, the AG cannot recover the tax from the shareholder, and the tax liability becomes a direct corporate debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving or failing to withhold are personally liable for the unpaid amount. Willful non-collection accompanied by false accounting constitutes tax fraud and subjects the responsible directors to criminal fines and imprisonment, including where ownership is held through foreign holding companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and retain a Local File or Master File despite cross-border intercompany transactions; embedding in-app user growth revenue into the Swiss entity's result without corresponding Swiss value creation; charging excessive management fees or license royalties to drain Swiss taxable profit; not using a valid approved TP methodology.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authorities may adjust income upward to an arm's-length position, deny deduction of the excessive part, reclassify the excess as a dividend subject to 35% WHT and issue a default assessment. Procedural fines up to CHF 10,000 apply; where contemporaneous documentation is absent, the taxpayer bears the burden and evidentiary losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign intercompany agreements with artificial prices are jointly and severally liable for resulting tax deficiencies, interest and penalties. Where a parent-company controller forces the Swiss entity into loss-making transfer prices, that individual can be treated as an accomplice to tax evasion and penalized personally, including by imprisonment.
